title: THE GOD WHO WAS ASKED TO CHOOSE
deck: A river god has not answered either of two opposing prayers in six weeks, and the valley is drying around its silence; nine days before the Lift, Illuminara walks the river with it and finds that nobody has ever asked for what they actually need.
shape: Seven scenes across twelve days: a dry riverbed and a god that cannot see past its next bend, a terrace with swept and useless gutters, a gravel channel full of eggs, a weir post and two columns on a slate, a night argument about who keeps a god's edges, a day of asking and six dawns of counting aloud, and a flood let up in three pinned stages that has to stay between its banks.

scenes.title: The Dry Bend
paragraphs: *The Veshra bed below the old weir · dawn of the first day*

Illuminara had been hired to measure a weir, and she had spent the night doing it: three sluice gates of black oak, the third rusted fast in its slot, a gauge post notched in hands from the pool floor to the lip. At first light she walked downstream to see where the water went, and the water went nowhere, because there was hardly any. The Veshra had shrunk to a brown thread. Where the bend should have run deep, something the height of a tall man stood in the cracked mud with its arms at its sides.
It looked like a very tired person. That was the kindest description she could make. Its edges were damp and did not hold.

**Oun**  
You are the survey. Pell said one would come. I would offer you water, but it is the one thing I am not giving anyone.

**Illuminara**  
Then I'll offer you my name. Illuminara. Are you the river?

**Oun**  
I am what answers to it. Oun. Six weeks I have heard two prayers and answered neither.

It opened one hand, and the two prayers came out of the air between them the way a name comes out of a crowd. From upstream, Upper Shale: *Oun, lift the river, our seed is thirsty.* From downstream, thinner and just as certain, Lowmere: *Oun, hold the river, our eggs are in the gravel.*

**Oun**  
One wants the river up and one wants it down. Do not tidy it. I have done that sum ten thousand times and it comes out as a drowned village.
She looked at the bed it stood in. Under the mud, in the shadow of a crack, ran a line of squared foundation stones.

**Oun**  
Aldmere. Two prayers then as well, and I chose. I reached past my banks to make the choosing good, and the river that reached came into its houses at night. I stand here because it is the one place that is entirely mine to be ashamed in.

**Illuminara**  
Where have you stood since?

**Oun**  
Nowhere. I am in the river, and I cannot see past the next bend of it. I hear prayers the way you would hear a shout from a house you have never been inside.

**Illuminara**  
Then walk it with me. Source to sea, on foot. The Lift is nine days off and you have six weeks of silence, and I would like to see what each of them is praying for before either of us decides what you owe.
Oun looked at its own hand for a while, as if checking that it was still attached.

**Oun**  
I have never walked it.

**Illuminara**  
I know. Mind the cracks.

scenes.title: Hill Water
paragraphs: *The Upper Shale terraces · the second day, mid-morning*

Six terrace lines climbed the hill above the weir, and the barley beds on them had gone the colour of old paper. Ketterin Osk met them at the lowest wall with a trowel in her belt and the stance of a woman who had been braced for visitors for six weeks. She saw the surveyor, not the damp tall shape at the surveyor's shoulder; Oun had asked to stay unseen until it knew what it was looking at.
Illuminara knelt and pushed her fingers into a bed. The crust broke in plates. Under it the soil was dry to the knuckle, then to the wrist.

**Ketterin Osk**  
The seed is gone by the sixth morning. Sown on the Lift's promise, like every year. My mother's mother lost a line to a late Lift and taught me to count mornings.

**Illuminara**  
What would stop the count?

**Ketterin Osk**  
Water standing a hand deep in the beds for five days, begun before the sixth morning. That is all the barley wants. The river is the only road we have ever had to ask for it, so we ask for the river.
Illuminara looked up the wall. At the top of every terrace a stone gutter ran from the hillside into the bed behind it, swept clean and bone dry.

**Illuminara**  
Somebody keeps those swept.

**Ketterin Osk**  
My duty, from my grandmother's. Hill drains, for hill water. Rain has never come on the hill in my life. It comes up the river, if at all.
At Illuminara's shoulder, Oun made a sound like gravel settling, and spoke for her alone.

**Oun**  
I do not rain on hills. A river god that rains on hills has forgotten where its banks are. That is how Aldmere began.

**Illuminara**  
Nobody has asked you to.

**Oun**  
Then no one has asked for anything I could do.
*She hasn't asked for a flood,* Illuminara thought. *She's asked for a number: a hand deep, five days. The flood is only the road she knew.*

scenes.title: Gravel
paragraphs: *The Lowmere spawning channels · dawn of the third day*

Lowmere's channels were shallow cuts of clean gravel beside the main bed, and under a hand of clear water the gravel glittered. Illuminara crouched before she understood why. Eggs, thousands of them, each the size of a lentil, each holding a dark fleck that would be a fish. She had watched galaxies resolve and had been steadier for it; this stopped her breath in a smaller, more dangerous way, as if she had stepped on something not meant to be seen and it had let her.
Daro Venn stood waist-deep at the channel mouth with a notched stick, reading the water the way a man reads a sleeping child's breathing.

**Daro Venn**  
Two hands of river at the weir, no more, and the channel runs gentle. Past two, the current lifts the gravel and the eggs go with it. Six days to hatch: the ninth morning. After that the fry need the river high, four hands for two days, to carry them over the bar before it closes. Everyone on the Veshra eats ashfin through the winter, even the ones upstream who think we steal their water.
Behind the surveyor, Oun was looking at the gravel. Illuminara had not seen it look at anything yet; it had only looked toward.

**Oun**  
I have been a river for ten thousand years, and I have never once seen an egg.

**Illuminara**  
You were never asked to look.

**Oun**  
I was asked to hold. I held. The barley wants a hand of water on a hill for five days. These want the river no higher than two until they hatch. Nobody has asked me for two things that cannot happen. They have asked me for one thing each, and I have heard them as a quarrel.

**Illuminara**  
Yes.

**Oun**  
Do not look so pleased. I still cannot rain on a hill.

scenes.title: Two Columns
paragraphs: *The old weir, the gauge post · evening of the third day*

Illuminara had chalked a slate and set it on the lip of the weir, and now four people stood around it in the last light: Ketterin Osk and Daro Venn, who had not stood within ten paces of each other since the spring, Pell the weir-keeper with his oil-can, and the surveyor. The sixth morning was three dawns off. Oun stood among them now, visible at last as a wet shimmer where the air was thicker. Nobody mentioned it. Everybody had decided not to be the first.
On the slate, in two columns:

*Upper Shale: a hand of water standing in the beds, five days, begun before the sixth morning. Lowmere: the river at two hands or under until the ninth morning; then four hands for two days. A finger either way is the post breathing. Past that, stop.*

**Ketterin Osk**  
So I am to trust that when my beds are wet your people will not simply open the weir and drain the pool.

**Daro Venn**  
And I am to trust my eggs to rain on a hill that has never rained. Last Lift your canal-takers held the weir three days past the mark and my channel ran silt for a week.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Because your nets choked the tail.

**Illuminara**  
I am not asking you to like each other. I am asking you to read two numbers off the same post. One of you stands at the pool and one at the tail. Over the line, either of you says stop. Not to me. To the water.

**Ketterin Osk**  
I can say stop for my lines. I cannot say yes for them. That is a vote, and I will not put a god to them in the dark.

**Daro Venn**  
Nor I for the nets.

**Pell**  
And who lifts gate three for the pulse? That gate has not moved in sixty years. If it lets go, it lets go all at once, onto Lowmere.

**Illuminara**  
Then it will not be allowed to. Oak pins in the guide post, at three hands, three and a half, four. The gate rises to a pin and no further, and you pull the pin, not I. An hour's hold at each, and the tail reads before you draw the next. If either watcher says stop, your pawl drops it to the pin below and Oun draws the river back. Your gate, its water, their word.

**Pell**  
It is my gate, and I want it said.

**Daro Venn**  
And if the god overshoots?
Oun spoke aloud for the first time to anyone but her. Its voice was low, and the pool shivered with it.

**Oun**  
I have overshot once. I would rather not discover that I can do it twice. I will answer you tomorrow. First I must speak to the surveyor about my banks.

scenes.title: Where My Banks Are
paragraphs: *The weir top, night · the same evening*

The pool was black and almost still. Pell had gone down to his gate with a lantern and his oil-can, muttering about slots. Oun stood at the edge of the stonework with its feet in the little water that remained.

**Oun**  
You have drawn two columns, and they fit. I can see that. Now I will tell you what the columns do not show. To rain on that hill, I must go past my banks, and I have done that once, and the village is a line of stones. Every mercy I give is a drought someone else is praying through. Tell me what you would give up.
Illuminara took the question as seriously as it was asked. She did not reach for comfort.

**Illuminara**  
The right to be the one who says where your banks are. I could. I could stand at the ridge and hold the border with my own body, and the rain would fall where I told it. And you would learn that someone else keeps your edges, and the next time no one was there, you would do what you did at Aldmere.

**Oun**  
Then who keeps them?

**Illuminara**  
The two who pray against each other. One on each bank, every dawn, reading the post. You were never wrong to love both. You were alone with a border.
For a time Oun did not answer. Under the stone, water ticked.

**Oun**  
There is a term I will add. They say where my banks are, aloud, each dawn, before any rain. And either may say stop, and I will stop, and neither will need the other's leave. If only one can say it, it is a leash on the other. And they say the name first. Aldmere. Every dawn. I will not rain on a hill for a village that has been left out of the count.

**Illuminara**  
That is a better rule than mine.

**Oun**  
I know. It is mine.

**Illuminara**  
One job I will do with my hands, and I say it now so nobody finds it out at the bend. If the flood comes to Aldmere with a head on it, it will swing for the oldest bed it remembers. I will go and look at what lies there. Whatever it is, it is timber or stone, not your border. Moving it is mine. Saying stop is theirs.

**Oun**  
Then we look together.
Down at the third gate, the lantern flickered, and Pell's voice came up the stonework, flat and clear.

**Pell**  
Slot is rough. I will not call it true until I have oiled it three nights. You will wait.

**Illuminara**  
I will wait.
It was, she reflected, the most useful sentence anyone had said to her all week.

scenes.title: The Count
paragraphs: *The weir, the terraces and the tail · the fourth to the ninth day*

The fourth day was for asking. Oun went up to the terrace-house at dusk and down to the net shed afterward, and said the same in both: what it would do, what it had done at Aldmere, and the word that would stop it. Both villages argued for the length of a lamp, and came to the post with their answers.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Upper Shale says yes to five days, not to a season. Nine lines for, three against. The three want the watcher chosen again every Lift, not handed down like a trowel.

**Oun**  
Then I am bound for a year, not an age. That is fair.

**Daro Venn**  
Fourteen nets say yes to the trial. Four say no, and will stand on the tail bank to watch, and I told them they may call stop as loud as I do. Old Maran's grandfather had a house at Aldmere. He wants the name said before the readings, not after. And the Lift is a second question. Lowmere will answer it on the ninth morning, with the eggs in front of it.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Then the name first, and the Lift unpromised.

**Oun**  
Both.
On the fifth dawn Ketterin Osk stood on the pool bank and Daro Venn on the tail, forty paces of grey water between them, and neither would look first.

**Daro Venn**  
Aldmere.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Aldmere. Here, at the post. One hand.

**Daro Venn**  
Here, at the tail. One hand and a finger.

Nothing happened for the space of ten breaths. Then the air over the Shale slope darkened along a line so straight that Illuminara laughed aloud. The rain fell as if drawn with a rule: heavy on the five upper terraces, nothing on the track beside them, a hard bright edge at the ridge where the cloud stopped as though it had been told. She stood on the weir with her head tipped back, a person watching weather do what weather did not do, wet to the collarbone and delighted.

The gutters, swept clean for three generations, ran for the first time in anyone's life. At the sixth dawn, the seed morning, Ketterin Osk's stake in the top bed stood a hand deep, and she cut the first of five notches into it. She walked the terraces from the top down, touching the walls, and stopped at the lowest. The sixth line sat in the lee of the ridge, and the rain that fed the five above it had passed overhead. She crouched there with her trowel and told the truth.

**Ketterin Osk**  
This one is lost. Half a soak is a rot.

**Daro Venn**  
Lowmere has seed barley in the granary. I will lend it to you for a second sowing.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Lend.

**Daro Venn**  
A sack back in the autumn, and you hold the weir mark with me for a season.

**Ketterin Osk**  
A sack and a half, and you keep your nets out of the tail.

**Daro Venn**  
Done.
Illuminara said nothing, and thought it was the most hopeful bargain she had witnessed in a year of far larger ones.

The count held. On the seventh night the wind shifted and the cloud edge slid a hundred paces toward the river; at the post the gauge crept to two hands and a finger. Daro Venn did not wait for anyone. He called into the dark.

**Daro Venn**  
Stop.
The rain stopped. It stopped in the middle of a drop, Ketterin Osk said afterwards, who had been under it.

**Ketterin Osk**  
It did not even ask me.

**Daro Venn**  
It did not ask me either. That was the term.

At the eighth dawn they chalked the ridge on the post, so that both of them could read the cloud, and began again, a morning's rain only. The tail read one hand and two fingers; the stake, a hand and a finger, and a third notch. On the ninth morning Daro Venn knelt in the gravel and held his stick very still. In every egg a dark fleck had grown a tail, and the tails were moving.

scenes.title: The Lift
paragraphs: *The old weir and the Aldmere bend · noon of the tenth day to noon of the twelfth*

Pell had called the slot true on the seventh morning, before witnesses, so that it could not later be said otherwise, and had oiled it every night since. The three oak pins sat in the guide post. On the ninth evening Illuminara and Oun had walked the Aldmere bend together and found what the river would swing toward: a jam of drowned timber in the old street-bed, heavy as a barn roof. It was on the slate now, under the two columns: *Jam: I lift it at the second hold, before the head comes. Stop is theirs.* Lowmere had answered the Lift that morning, eleven nets to seven. The seven stood on the tail bank with their hands raised to say stop, and none of them did.

**Pell**  
First pin.

He drew it. The gate rose a third of its span and stopped on the next, and sixty years of rust gave up along a line Illuminara could have drawn with her eyes shut. The pool ran out under it, brown and then white.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Three hands.

**Daro Venn**  
Three. The gravel is staying.

They held an hour. At the second pin, with the river at three and a half, Illuminara went down the bank in four strides and stood in the Aldmere bend. The water leaned on her. She took the jam in both hands, the great sodden mass of it, and set it on the bank with a care she would have used for a sleeping animal.
Oun stood at the stones beside her and did not move.

**Oun**  
It wanted to swing there. I could feel it wanting.
The river stood at three and a half for the second hour. Then Daro Venn waded out to the tail mark, read his stick against the post, and called it across the water.

**Daro Venn**  
Three and a half at the tail, and the gravel holding. Lowmere says proceed.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Upper Shale says proceed. We are not past a finger.

**Pell**  
Pawl is set. If either of you says stop, it drops the gate to this pin before the word is out, and Oun needs one breath to draw the river back. Third pin.
At the third pin the head of the flood came down, and found no door where it had expected one, and ran between its banks.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Four hands!

**Daro Venn**  
Four and a finger! That is the post breathing. Say it again anyway!

**Ketterin Osk**  
Four and a finger! Here! This is the bank!

**Daro Venn**  
And here!

**Oun**  
I felt it. I felt where the banks were. They were not mine. They were being said.

Down the Lowmere channels went a silver thread of fry, carried out on the Lift, over the bar, into the lagoon. Both villages had come down to the water, and for the first time in six weeks they prayed in one voice, not for the river up or the river down, but for the river to stay where it was told.

The pulse held through the night. On the eleventh dawn Ketterin Osk read her stake before she read the post: five notches, a hand deep, five days standing. At noon of the twelfth day Pell let the gate down pin by pin, and Oun drew the river in behind it, and the tail read two hands, and the fry were over the bar.

By dusk the sixth line stood bare and dark, ready for a second sowing in lent seed, and on the dry bend where Aldmere had been, someone had begun to set a stone upright, and someone else had begun to chalk a name on it, and neither of them was the same someone.

**Oun**  
Say it again, tomorrow, at dawn.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Aldmere. Here.

**Daro Venn**  
Aldmere. And here.

**Illuminara**  
And Aldmere.

Oun looked at the three of them for a long time, with the plain astonishment of a being that has just seen the other side of its own river, and then it walked downstream to find out what was past the next bend.

critic_line: Illuminara helps Oun understand that the two villages are asking for bounded, measurable needs rather than a divine choice between winners, then protects a staged and freely governed release in which Oun, both communities and Pell retain the right to stop.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1; genuine independent GPT and Claude judgments; exact equal 50/50 arithmetic mean.
shared_strengths: Humane, dialogue-driven fable with a clear idea: reframe a quarrel as two specific requests, and let the people who pray against each other keep the god's banks. Concrete numbers, a small honest loss, and a warm ending. Procedural mid-section and tidy resolution may lose some.

The vulnerable river god, humane dialogue, and tangible stakes give an abstract conflict emotional life. Shared authority becomes a satisfying dramatic resolution, with losses and dissent preserved. Repeated measurements and procedural safeguards may slow pleasure reading, while the unusually capable surveyor and explicit lessons occasionally make the outcome feel engineered.
shared_reservations: Illuminara had chalked a slate and set it on the lip of the weir, and now four people stood around it in the last light: Ketterin Osk and Daro Venn
An hour's hold at each, and the tail reads before you draw the next.

translation_sl.title: BOG, KI SO GA PROSILI, NAJ IZBERE
translation_sl.deck: Rečni bog že šest tednov ni odgovoril na nobeno od dveh nasprotujočih si molitev in dolina se suši okoli njegovega molka; devet dni pred Dvigom Illuminara z njim prehodi reko in odkrije, da nihče še nikoli ni prosil za tisto, kar v resnici potrebuje.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v dvanajstih dneh: suha rečna struga in bog, ki ne vidi čez naslednji rečni zavoj, terasa s pometenimi, a neuporabnimi žlebovi, prodnat kanal, poln iker, jezovni merilni steber in dva stolpca na tablici, nočni spor o tem, kdo varuje robove boga, dan spraševanja in šest juter glasnega štetja ter poplava, spuščena v treh stopnjah z zatiči, ki mora ostati med svojima bregovoma.

scenes.title: Suhi zavoj
paragraphs: *Struga Veshre pod starim jezom · svit prvega dne*

Illuminara je bila najeta, da izmeri jez, in s tem je preživela noč: tri zapornice iz črnega hrasta, tretja zarjavela in negibno ujeta v svojem utoru, merilni steber z zarezami v dlaneh od dna tolmuna do roba. Ob prvi svetlobi je odšla po toku navzdol, da bi videla, kam odteka voda, vendar voda ni odtekala nikamor, ker je skoraj ni bilo. Veshra se je skrčila v rjavo nit. Tam, kjer bi moral biti zavoj globok, je v razpokani glini z rokama ob telesu stalo nekaj, visoko kakor visok človek.
Videti je bilo kakor zelo utrujen človek. To je bil najprijaznejši opis, ki ga je zmogla. Njegovi robovi so bili vlažni in niso držali oblike.

**Oun**  
Ti si meritev. Pell je rekel, da bo nekdo prišel. Ponudil bi ti vodo, vendar je to edino, česar ne dajem nikomur.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ti ponudim svoje ime. Illuminara. Si ti reka?

**Oun**  
Jaz sem tisto, kar se odzove nanjo. Oun. Šest tednov poslušam dve molitvi in nisem odgovoril na nobeno.

Razprl je dlan in molitvi sta se pojavili v zraku med njima tako, kakor se iz množice pojavi ime. Od zgoraj, iz Upper Shale: *Oun, dvigni reko, naše seme je žejno.* Od spodaj, iz Lowmere, tišja in prav tako odločna: *Oun, zadrži reko, naše ikre so v produ.*

**Oun**  
Eni hočejo reko višje, drugi nižje. Ne olepšuj tega. Ta račun sem izračunal deset tisočkrat in rezultat je utopljena vas.
Pogledala je strugo, v kateri je stal. Pod glino je v senci razpoke tekla vrsta klesanih temeljnih kamnov.

**Oun**  
Aldmere. Tudi tedaj sta bili dve molitvi in izbral sem. Segel sem prek svojih bregov, da bi bila izbira dobra, reka, ki sem jo poslal, pa je ponoči vstopila v njihove hiše. Tu stojim, ker je to edini kraj, kjer je moj sram povsem moj.

**Illuminara**  
Kje si stal od takrat?

**Oun**  
Nikjer. Sem v reki in ne vidim čez njen naslednji zavoj. Molitve slišim tako, kakor bi ti slišala krik iz hiše, v kateri še nikoli nisi bila.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jo prehodi z menoj. Od izvira do morja, peš. Do Dviga je devet dni, za teboj pa je šest tednov molka; rada bi videla, za kaj pravzaprav molijo, preden se kdorkoli od naju odloči, kaj jim dolguješ.
Oun je nekaj časa gledal svojo dlan, kakor da preverja, ali je še vedno pritrjena nanj.

**Oun**  
Nikoli je nisem prehodil.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. Pazi na razpoke.

scenes.title: Voda za hrib
paragraphs: *Terase Upper Shale · drugi dan, sredi dopoldneva*

Šest vrst teras se je vzpenjalo po hribu nad jezom, ječmenove grede na njih pa so dobile barvo starega papirja. Ketterin Osk ju je pričakala pri najnižjem zidu z zidarsko lopatico za pasom in držo ženske, ki se je šest tednov pripravljala na obiskovalce. Videla je geodetinjo, ne pa vlažne visoke postave ob njeni rami; Oun je prosil, naj ostane neviden, dokler ne bo razumel, kaj gleda.
Illuminara je pokleknila in porinila prste v gredo. Skorja se je lomila v ploščah. Pod njo je bila zemlja suha do členkov, nato do zapestja.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Seme je izgubljeno do šestega jutra. Posejano je bilo na obljubo Dviga, kakor vsako leto. Mati moje matere je zaradi poznega Dviga izgubila eno vrsto in me naučila šteti jutra.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi ustavilo štetje?

**Ketterin Osk**  
Voda, ki bi pet dni stala eno dlan globoko v gredah in bi prišla pred šestim jutrom. To je vse, kar ječmen potrebuje. Reka je edina pot, po kateri smo lahko kadar koli prosili zanjo, zato prosimo za reko.
Illuminara je pogledala po zidu navzgor. Na vrhu vsake terase je kamnit žleb vodil s pobočja v gredo za njim, pometen do čistega in suh kakor kost.

**Illuminara**  
Nekdo skrbi, da so ti žlebovi pometeni.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Moja dolžnost, podedovana od babice. Hribovski odtoki za hribovsko vodo. Dež na hribu ni padel še nikoli v mojem življenju. Če sploh pride, pride po reki navzgor.
Ob Illuminarini rami je Oun zazvenel kakor polegajoči se prod in spregovoril samo zanjo.

**Oun**  
Na hribih ne dežujem. Rečni bog, ki dežuje na hribih, je pozabil, kje so njegovi bregovi. Tako se je začel Aldmere.

**Illuminara**  
Nihče te ni prosil za to.

**Oun**  
Potem nihče ni prosil za nič, kar bi lahko storil.
*Ni prosila za poplavo,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Prosila je za število: dlan globoko, pet dni. Poplava je bila le edina pot, ki jo je poznala.*

scenes.title: Prod
paragraphs: *Drstitveni kanali Lowmere · svit tretjega dne*

Kanali Lowmere so bili plitve zareze čistega proda ob glavni strugi in prod se je bleščal pod dlanjo bistre vode. Illuminara je počepnila, preden je razumela zakaj. Ikre, na tisoče, vsaka velika kakor leča in v vsaki temna pikica, iz katere bo nastala riba. Opazovala je razreševanje galaksij in pri tem ostala mirnejša; to ji je vzelo sapo na manjši, nevarnejši način, kakor da je stopila na nekaj, česar ne bi smela videti, pa ji je to dovolilo.
Daro Venn je stal do pasu v vodi ob ustju kanala z zarezano palico in bral vodo tako, kakor človek bere dihanje spečega otroka.

**Daro Venn**  
Dve dlani reke pri jezu, nič več, pa kanal teče nežno. Nad dvema tok dvigne prod in ikre odnese z njim. Šest dni do izvalitve: deveto jutro. Nato mladice potrebujejo visoko reko, štiri dlani dva dni, da jih ponese čez pregrado, preden se zapre. Vsi ob Veshri pozimi jedo pepelne ribe, tudi tisti zgoraj, ki mislijo, da jim krademo vodo.
Za geodetinjo je Oun gledal prod. Illuminara ga še ni videla pogledati ničesar; doslej je gledal le proti nečemu.

**Oun**  
Reka sem že deset tisoč let in še nikoli nisem videl ikre.

**Illuminara**  
Nikoli te niso prosili, da pogledaš.

**Oun**  
Prosili so me, naj zadržim. Zadržal sem. Ječmen potrebuje dlan vode na hribu pet dni. Te ikre potrebujejo reko največ dve dlani visoko, dokler se ne izvalijo. Nihče me ni prosil za dve stvari, ki se ne moreta zgoditi. Vsak me je prosil za eno stvar, jaz pa sem ju slišal kot prepir.

**Illuminara**  
Da.

**Oun**  
Ne bodi videti tako zadovoljna. Še vedno ne morem deževati na hribu.

scenes.title: Dva stolpca
paragraphs: *Stari jez, merilni steber · večer tretjega dne*

Illuminara je s kredo popisala tablico in jo postavila na rob jezu, zdaj pa so v zadnji svetlobi okoli nje stali štirje: Ketterin Osk in Daro Venn, ki od pomladi nista stala manj kot deset korakov drug od drugega, jezovni čuvaj Pell s svojo oljnico in geodetinja. Do šestega jutra so ostali trije sviti. Oun je zdaj stal med njimi, naposled viden kot moker migljaj, kjer je bil zrak gostejši. Nihče tega ni omenil. Vsi so se odločili, da ne bodo prvi.
Na tablici, v dveh stolpcih:

*Upper Shale: dlan vode, ki pet dni stoji v gredah, z začetkom pred šestim jutrom. Lowmere: reka pri dveh dlaneh ali nižje do devetega jutra; nato štiri dlani za dva dni. Prst v eno ali drugo smer je dihanje stebra. Čez to mejo se ustavi.*

**Ketterin Osk**  
Torej naj zaupam, da vaši ljudje, ko bodo moje grede mokre, ne bodo preprosto odprli jezu in izpraznili tolmuna.

**Daro Venn**  
Jaz pa naj svoje ikre zaupam dežju na hribu, kjer še nikoli ni deževalo. Ob zadnjem Dvigu so vaši upravljavci kanalov zadrževali jez odprt tri dni čez oznako in moj kanal je teden dni nosil mulj.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Ker so vaše mreže zadušile odtok.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prosim vaju, da se imata rada. Prosim vaju, da odčitata dve števili z istega stebra. Eden stoji pri tolmunu, drugi pri iztoku. Če gre čez črto, lahko kdorkoli od vaju reče stop. Ne meni. Vodi.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Za svoje vrste lahko rečem stop. Ne morem pa namesto njih reči da. O tem se glasuje in boga jim ne bom pripeljala v temi.

**Daro Venn**  
Tudi jaz ne bom govoril za ribiče.

**Pell**  
In kdo dvigne tretjo zapornico za val? Ta vrata se niso premaknila šestdeset let. Če popustijo, popustijo vsa naenkrat, naravnost proti Lowmere.

**Illuminara**  
Tega jim ne bomo dovolili. Hrastovi zatiči v vodilnem stebru, pri treh dlaneh, treh in pol, štirih. Zapornica se dvigne do zatiča in nič dlje, zatič pa izvlečeš ti, ne jaz. Na vsaki stopnji eno uro zadržimo in iztok se odčita, preden izvlečeš naslednjega. Če katerikoli opazovalec reče stop, tvoja zaskočka spusti zapornico do zatiča pod njo, Oun pa reko potegne nazaj. Tvoja vrata, njegova voda, njuna beseda.

**Pell**  
To so moja vrata in hočem, da je to izrečeno.

**Daro Venn**  
Kaj pa, če bog preseže mero?
Oun je prvič spregovoril na glas komurkoli razen njej. Njegov glas je bil globok in tolmun se je ob njem stresel.

**Oun**  
Enkrat sem presegel mero. Raje ne bi odkril, da to zmorem dvakrat. Odgovoril vam bom jutri. Najprej moram z geodetinjo govoriti o svojih bregovih.

scenes.title: Kje so moji bregovi
paragraphs: *Vrh jezu, noč · isti večer*
Tolmun je bil črn in skoraj negiben. Pell je odšel k zapornici z laterno in oljnico ter mrmral o utorih. Oun je stal na robu kamnitega zidu z nogami v tisti mali količini vode, ki je še ostala.

**Oun**  
Narisala si dva stolpca in ujemata se. To vidim. Zdaj ti bom povedal, česa stolpca ne kažeta. Da dežujem na tistem hribu, moram iti prek svojih bregov; to sem že storil in vas je postala vrsta kamnov. Vsaka milost, ki jo dam, je suša, skozi katero moli nekdo drug. Povej mi, čemu bi se ti odpovedala.
Illuminara je vprašanje vzela tako resno, kakor je bilo zastavljeno. Ni segla po tolažbi.

**Illuminara**  
Pravici, da jaz odločam, kje so tvoji bregovi. Lahko bi. Lahko bi stala na grebenu in mejo držala z lastnim telesom, dež pa bi padal, kamor bi mu ukazala. Ti bi se naučil, da nekdo drug varuje tvoje robove, in naslednjič, ko tam ne bi bilo nikogar, bi storil to, kar si storil Aldmereju.

**Oun**  
Kdo jih bo potem varoval?

**Illuminara**  
Tista dva, ki molita drug proti drugemu. Vsak na svojem bregu, vsako jutro, ko bereta steber. Nikoli se nisi motil, ker si imel rad oba. Le sam si bil z mejo.
Oun nekaj časa ni odgovoril. Pod kamnom je kapljala voda.

**Oun**  
Dodal bom pogoj. Vsako jutro pred dežjem na glas povesta, kje so moji bregovi. Kdorkoli lahko reče stop, jaz pa bom ustavil, ne da bi potreboval dovoljenje drugega. Če to lahko reče samo eden, je to povodec na drugem. In najprej izgovorita ime. Aldmere. Vsako jutro. Ne bom deževal na hribu za vas, ki je bila izpuščena iz štetja.

**Illuminara**  
To je boljše pravilo od mojega.

**Oun**  
Vem. Moje je.

**Illuminara**  
Eno delo bom opravila s svojimi rokami in to povem zdaj, da tega nihče ne odkrije šele na zavoju. Če poplavni val pride do Aldmereja z grebenom, bo zavil proti najstarejši strugi, ki se je spomni. Šla bom pogledat, kaj leži tam. Karkoli je, je les ali kamen, ne tvoja meja. Premakniti to je moje delo. Reči stop je njuno.

**Oun**  
Potem pogledava skupaj.
Spodaj pri tretji zapornici je laterna zatrepetala in Pellov glas se je po kamnitem zidu dvignil raven in jasen.

**Pell**  
Utor je hrapav. Ne bom rekel, da je varen, dokler ga ne bom mazal tri noči. Počakali boste.

**Illuminara**  
Počakala bom.
Pomislila je, da je bil to najkoristnejši stavek, ki ji ga je kdorkoli izrekel ves teden.

scenes.title: Štetje
paragraphs: *Jez, terase in iztok · od četrtega do devetega dne*

Četrti dan je bil namenjen vprašanjem. Oun je ob mraku odšel do hiše na terasi in nato do ribiške lope ter v obeh krajih povedal isto: kaj bo storil, kaj je storil Aldmereju in katera beseda ga bo ustavila. Obe vasi sta se prepirali ves čas gorenja ene svetilke, nato pa prišli k stebru s svojima odgovoroma.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Upper Shale je rekel da petim dnem, ne celemu letnemu času. Devet vrst za, tri proti. Tiste tri hočejo, da opazovalca ob vsakem Dvigu izberemo znova, ne pa da se dolžnost deduje kakor zidarska lopatica.

**Oun**  
Potem sem zavezan za eno leto, ne za večnost. To je pravično.

**Daro Venn**  
Štirinajst ribičev je za preizkus. Štirje so proti in bodo stali na bregu pri iztoku ter opazovali; povedal sem jim, da lahko zavpijejo stop prav tako glasno kakor jaz. Ded starega Marana je imel hišo v Aldmereju. Hoče, da ime izgovorimo pred odčitki, ne po njih. Dvig pa je drugo vprašanje. Lowmere bo nanj odgovoril deveto jutro, pred ikrami.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Potem najprej ime, Dvig pa ni obljubljen.

**Oun**  
Oboje.
Ob petem svitu je Ketterin Osk stala na bregu tolmuna, Daro Venn pa pri iztoku; med njima je bilo štirideset korakov sive vode in nobeden ni hotel pogledati prvi.

**Daro Venn**  
Aldmere.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Aldmere. Tukaj, pri stebru. Ena dlan.

**Daro Venn**  
Tukaj, pri iztoku. Ena dlan in en prst.

Deset vdihov se ni zgodilo nič. Nato je zrak nad pobočjem Shale potemnel po črti, tako ravni, da se je Illuminara glasno zasmejala. Dež je padal, kakor bi bil narisan z ravnilom: močno na pet zgornjih teras, nič na stezo ob njih, oster svetel rob na grebenu, kjer se je oblak ustavil, kakor bi mu nekdo tako ukazal. Stala je na jezu z glavo nagnjeno nazaj, človek, ki gleda vreme početi tisto, česar vreme ne počne, mokra do ključnice in navdušena.

Žlebovi, tri generacije pometani do čistega, so prvič v življenju kogarkoli stekli. Ob šestem svitu, jutru semena, je kol Ketterin Osk v najvišji gredi stal dlan globoko in vanj je zarezala prvo od petih zarez. Prehodila je terase od vrha navzdol, se dotikala zidov in se ustavila pri najnižji. Šesta vrsta je ležala v zavetrju grebena in dež, ki je napajal pet višjih, je šel čeznjo. Počepnila je s svojo lopatico in povedala resnico.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Ta je izgubljena. Polovična namočitev pomeni gnitje.

**Daro Venn**  
Lowmere ima semenski ječmen v kašči. Posodil ti ga bom za drugo setev.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Posodil.

**Daro Venn**  
Jeseni vrneš vrečo in eno sezono z menoj držiš jezovno oznako.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Vrečo in pol, ti pa svoje mreže umakneš iz iztoka.

**Daro Venn**  
Dogovorjeno.
Illuminara ni rekla ničesar in pomislila je, da je bil to najbolj obetaven dogovor, ki mu je bila priča v letu veliko večjih dogovorov.

Štetje je držalo. Sedmo noč se je veter obrnil in rob oblaka je zdrsnil sto korakov proti reki; pri stebru se je merilnik povzpel do dveh dlani in enega prsta. Daro Venn ni čakal nikogar. Zaklical je v temo.

**Daro Venn**  
Stop.
Dež je prenehal. Ustavil se je sredi kaplje, je pozneje povedala Ketterin Osk, ki je stala pod njim.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Niti vprašal me ni.

**Daro Venn**  
Tudi mene ni vprašal. Tak je bil pogoj.

Ob osmem svitu sta na steber s kredo narisala greben, da bi oba lahko brala oblak, in začela znova, samo za eno dopoldne dežja. Iztok je kazal eno dlan in dva prsta; kol dlan in en prst ter tretjo zarezo. Deveto jutro je Daro Venn pokleknil v produ in svojo palico držal povsem mirno. V vsaki ikri je temni pikici zrasel rep in repi so se premikali.

scenes.title: Dvig
paragraphs: *Stari jez in zavoj pri Aldmereju · od poldneva desetega dne do poldneva dvanajstega*

Pell je sedmo jutro pred pričami razglasil utor za varnega, da pozneje ne bi mogel nihče trditi drugače, in odtlej ga je mazal vsako noč. Trije hrastovi zatiči so sedeli v vodilnem stebru. Deveti večer sta Illuminara in Oun skupaj prehodila zavoj pri Aldmereju in našla tisto, proti čemur bi reka zavila: gmoto potopljenega lesa v stari ulični strugi, težko kakor streha skednja. Zdaj je bilo zapisano na tablici pod obema stolpcema: *Zastoj: dvignem ga ob drugem zadržku, preden pride greben vala. Stop je njun.* Lowmere je tisto jutro odgovoril na vprašanje o Dvigu, enajst ribičev proti sedmim. Sedmerica je stala na bregu pri iztoku z dvignjenimi rokami, pripravljena reči stop, vendar ni tega rekel nihče.

**Pell**  
Prvi zatič.

Izvlekel ga je. Zapornica se je dvignila za tretjino svoje višine in se ustavila na naslednjem, šestdeset let rje pa je popustilo vzdolž črte, ki bi jo Illuminara lahko narisala z zaprtimi očmi. Tolmun je pod njo stekel, najprej rjav in nato bel.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Tri dlani.

**Daro Venn**  
Tri. Prod ostaja na mestu.

Zadržali so eno uro. Pri drugem zatiču, ko je bila reka pri treh dlaneh in pol, je Illuminara v štirih korakih prišla po bregu navzdol in stopila v zavoj pri Aldmereju. Voda se je uprla vanjo. Z obema rokama je prijela zastoj, veliko premočeno gmoto, in jo položila na breg tako previdno, kakor bi ravnala s spečo živaljo.
Oun je stal pri kamnih ob njej in se ni premaknil.

**Oun**  
Hotela je zaviti tja. Čutil sem, kako je hotela.
Reka je drugo uro stala pri treh dlaneh in pol. Nato je Daro Venn zabredel do oznake pri iztoku, odčital svojo palico glede na steber in zaklical čez vodo.

**Daro Venn**  
Tri in pol pri iztoku, prod drži. Lowmere dovoli nadaljevanje.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Upper Shale dovoli nadaljevanje. Meje nismo presegli niti za prst.

**Pell**  
Zaskočka je nastavljena. Če kdorkoli od vaju reče stop, spusti zapornico do tega zatiča, še preden je beseda izrečena do konca, Oun pa potrebuje en vdih, da reko potegne nazaj. Tretji zatič.
Pri tretjem zatiču je prišel greben poplavnega vala, ni našel vrat tam, kjer jih je pričakoval, in stekel je med bregovoma.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Štiri dlani!

**Daro Venn**  
Štiri in en prst! To je dihanje stebra. Vseeno povej še enkrat!

**Ketterin Osk**  
Štiri in en prst! Tukaj! To je breg!

**Daro Venn**  
In tukaj!

**Oun**  
Čutil sem ga. Čutil sem, kje so bregovi. Niso bili moji. Izgovarjali so jih.

Po kanalih Lowmere je stekla srebrna nit mladic, ki jih je Dvig ponesel čez pregrado in v laguno. Obe vasi sta prišli k vodi in prvič v šestih tednih molili z enim glasom: ne za reko višje ali reko nižje, temveč naj reka ostane tam, kjer ji je bilo rečeno.

Val je držal vso noč. Ob enajstem svitu je Ketterin Osk prebrala svoj kol, preden je prebrala steber: pet zarez, dlan globoko, pet dni stoječe vode. Opoldne dvanajstega dne je Pell spustil zapornico zatič za zatičem, Oun je za njo povlekel reko vase, iztok je kazal dve dlani in mladice so bile čez pregrado.

Do mraka je šesta vrsta stala gola in temna, pripravljena na drugo setev s posojenim semenom; na suhem zavoju, kjer je nekoč stal Aldmere, je nekdo začel postavljati kamen pokonci, nekdo drug pa nanj s kredo pisati ime, in to nista bila ista človeka.

**Oun**  
Jutri ob svitu povejte še enkrat.

**Ketterin Osk**  
Aldmere. Tukaj.

**Daro Venn**  
Aldmere. In tukaj.

**Illuminara**  
In Aldmere.
Oun jih je dolgo gledal z odkritim začudenjem bitja, ki je pravkar videlo drugo stran lastne reke, nato pa je odšel po toku navzdol, da bi izvedel, kaj leži za naslednjim zavojem.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara Ounu pomaga razumeti, da vasi prosita za omejene in merljive potrebe, ne pa za božansko izbiro med zmagovalci; nato zaščiti postopen in svobodno upravljan izpust, pri katerem Oun, obe skupnosti in Pell obdržijo pravico, da ga ustavijo.
